title: Guided request funnel and SLA lanes for enterprise analytics & export asks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define a guided funnel in the Console for enterprise customers to submit analytics, cost breakdown, and export/dashboard requests, plus a lightweight prioritization and SLA lane assignment process so PM/Eng can triage consistently and SLAs for committed deliverables are clear.
background: We receive high-volume ad hoc requests from enterprise customers for custom usage exports, granular cost breakdowns, and dashboarding support. Current handling is ad hoc (email/CS notes) leading to long lead times and inconsistent prioritization. This initiative standardizes intake, creates scoring lanes, and maps lanes to time-to-first-response and delivery expectations.
scope: Build Console request form and backend classification rules; define a scoring rubric and SLA lanes; operational runbook for assignment and reporting. Provide initial automation for routing to Solutions Eng, Analytics, or Product. Pilot with top 10 enterprise customers.
out_of_scope: Full self-serve dashboard builder, building custom dashboards for every request, major data warehouse integrations beyond CSV/Parquet exports.
intake_flow: 1) Console: 'Request analytics or export' entry point visible to workspace admins
2) Guided form: purpose, dataset scope, time window, anonymization needs, export format, urgency, business impact, attach example queries
3) Auto-classifier: map to request type (export, dashboard, cost-decomposition, billing dispute) and propose SLA lane
4) Assign: auto-assign to Solutions Eng for discovery or to Analytics backlog for scheduled work
5) Notify: customer receives estimated response time and required clarifying questions
6) Tracking: request generates a ticket in Linear and a row in a triage dashboard for PM/SE rotation
prioritization_rubric: Score axes: customer_tier (1-5), revenue_risk (0-5), security/compliance (0-5), time_sensitivity (0-5), reusability (0-5)
Weighting: customer_tier*0.3 + revenue_risk*0.25 + security*0.2 + time_sensitivity*0.15 + reusability*0.1

Interpretation: Score >= 12 -> SLA lane A (24h response, committed scope delivery 2 weeks), 8-11 -> lane B (3 business days triage, delivery 4-8 weeks), <8 -> lane C (self-serve guidance + monthly backlog review)
Manual override: PM can escalate to a higher lane with justification; SE can request de-escalation if scope unclear
sla_tiers: Lane A - Enterprise SLA: Initial acknowledgement within 24 hours, discovery call within 3 business days, committed deliverable timeline defined in kickoff (usually <= 2 weeks)
Lane B - High priority: Acknowledgement within 3 business days, scoping within 2 weeks, delivery windows depend on backlog (4-8 weeks)
Lane C - Low priority / Self-serve: Template guidance and export tools provided; request reviewed during monthly backlog grooming for potential inclusion
console_form_spec: Fields: request_title, brief_summary (200 chars), dataset_scope (dropdown+free text), start_date, end_date, required_fields_for_export, format_preference (CSV/Parquet/Redshift copy), privacy_constraints, contact_person, desired_due_date
Guidance UX: inline examples, suggested presets for common asks (monthly usage export, per-route cost breakdown, workspace-level embeddings usage)
Attachments: allow sample CSVs, dashboard mockups, SQL queries
Validation: required fields: dataset_scope, business_impact, contact_person
Access control: only workspace admins or billing contacts can submit enterprise SLA requests
acceptance_criteria: Console form implemented behind feature flag in staging
Auto-classifier rules return a lane suggestion with >70% precision in pilot set
Linear ticket creation with mapped labels and assignment works end-to-end
Triage dashboard shows live queue, SLA lane, owner, and score
Pilot with 10 pilot customers completed and feedback logged
